title: Three Sooners Share OU's Single-Game Receiving TD Record
question: What is Oklahoma's single-game record for touchdown catches, and who holds it?
answer: Oklahoma's single-game record is four touchdown receptions, shared by Trent Smith (Kansas, 2001), Jermaine Gresham (Texas A&M, 2007) and Kenny Stills (West Virginia, 2012).
summary: Four touchdown catches in one game is the Oklahoma record, shared by Trent Smith, Jermaine Gresham and Kenny Stills across three different decades.
body: Oklahoma's single-game record for touchdown receptions is four, and three different Sooners have reached it. Tight end Trent Smith got there first on Oct. 13, 2001, in a 38-10 win over Kansas, when he also caught 11 passes. Both numbers were school records at that point, according to OU's game coverage.

Jermaine Gresham tied the mark on Nov. 3, 2007, in Norman. Sam Bradford threw five touchdown passes in a 42-14 win over Texas A&M, and four of them went to Gresham, who finished with five catches for 80 yards. Texas A&M's own recap of the game described his four scores as tying Smith's school record.

Wide receiver Kenny Stills became the third on Nov. 17, 2012, at West Virginia. In a 50-49 shootout in Morgantown, he caught four touchdown passes from Landry Jones, and Oklahoma needed every one of them to survive a game that swung back and forth until the final minutes. OU's notes from that game listed his performance as tying the school record shared by Gresham and Smith.

Nobody has gone past four since. Oklahoma's statistical leaders list still shows the single-game receiving touchdown record as a three-way tie across 2001, 2007 and 2012. It is a good bit of trivia because the three players were so different: a tall tight end in the early Stoops years, a tight end who became a first-round pick, and a receiver who thrived in the Landry Jones era.
This list reflects the records as published in the sources below. Fans who want to see whether a future Sooner reaches five can check the official OU record book.
